blocks.text: Once it was established that genes are the units of inheritance, that genes are located on chromosomes, and that chromosomes are made of DNA and proteins, scientists tried to find out whether genes are made of DNA, of protein or of both. It took almost 30 years, from the 1920s to the 1950s, to answer this question.

blocks.title: Information: what a genetic material must do
blocks.text: A molecule that serves as genetic material must be able to code for the sequence of amino acids in proteins, replicate itself before cell division, be present in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells, and change over time to account for evolution. Only one molecule, DNA, fulfils all these requirements.

blocks.prompt: List two properties a genetic material must have.
blocks.explanation: Any two of: it codes for the amino acid sequence of proteins; it replicates before division; it is in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells; it can change over time.

items: Question of the 1920s-1950s: are genes DNA, protein or both?
Genetic material must code, replicate, sit in the nucleus and be able to change.
